observations: Photo 0 is a tight close-up of the top of a sewing machine head casing.
Red-and-white decal reads 'EM81' matching the seller's claimed 'Emel' brand.
A large balance wheel and bobbin-winder assembly is visible on the right side, typical of industrial machine heads.
No view of the full machine body, needle plate, motor, pedal, or table/stand.
No stitching sample, power cord, or motor (servo/clutch) visible anywhere in the frame.

identity.kind: industrial sewing machine (head only, as shown)

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows only the top casing; no motor or drive mechanism is visible to confirm direct-drive vs clutch/belt motor.
Photo 0 decal clearly reads 'EM81' with stylized branding.

claims.claim: Industrial sewing machine (implied full working set)
claims.evidence: Only the head's top corner is shown; no table, stand, motor, or pedal visible to confirm it is a complete industrial setup.

risks.risk: Motor type (direct-drive servo vs older clutch/belt) unconfirmed, which affects value significantly.
risks.proof: Photo of the underside of the machine showing the mounted motor and belt/direct coupling.
risks.if_unproven: priced as basic clutch-motor type, not direct-drive

risks.risk: Completeness of set (table, stand, motor, pedal) unknown.
risks.proof: Wide shot of the entire machine including table and motor.
risks.if_unproven: priced as head-only, no table/motor included

risks.risk: Working condition (stitch quality, motor function, wiring) cannot be assessed from a static close-up.
risks.proof: Short video of the machine running and sewing a test seam.

risks.risk: Cosmetic condition of the rest of the housing (cracks, rust, missing parts) hidden outside the cropped frame.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming visible wear consistent with heavy use

proof_requests: Wide photo showing the entire machine, table, and motor together.
Close-up of the motor and drive mechanism underneath the table.
Short video of the machine powered on and stitching.
Photo of the full body/housing from the front and side to check for damage.
response.reason: The single photo only shows a small corner of the machine's top casing confirming the brand and model, but gives no view of the motor, table, or overall completeness needed to set even a worst-case price for an 'industrial' and 'direct drive' claim.
